reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and, consistent with that, the redline is byte-identical to the originals and no counterparty comment is proposed — nothing is raised as a negotiation issue.

The cited text supports compliance: Section 7.1.1 leaves each Party owning its own background and generated IP (no assignment of AbbVie IP to Harpoon), Section 3.8.2(c) vests sole ownership of all Regulatory Documentation, Regulatory Approvals and Product Labeling in AbbVie with a Harpoon further-assurances/assignment covenant, and Section 5.2 gives Harpoon only a narrow non-exclusive, non-sublicensable licence limited to its Initial Development Plan obligations.

Joint ownership under Section 7.1.2 is expressly paired with each Party's right to Exploit the Joint Intellectual Property Rights 'without a duty of seeking consent from or accounting to the other Party', so it sits outside the rule's walk-away ('joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit'); the rationale correctly identifies and reasons through this.

Section 12.7.1 is a royalty-bearing reversion licence (not an assignment) of AbbVie Reversion IP, expressly excluding other AbbVie Patents/Know-How, so it does not transfer ownership of our IP; the rationale flags the redactions as noted-not-flagged, which matches the playbook's treatment of minor/unverifiable sub-elements.
Deterministic check ('no assignment of Customer Data/IP to Vendor remains') passes, and no changed-character concern arises since there is no edit.

Minor accuracy point only: the rationale labels the allocation as meeting the 'preferred' position although the preferred wording calls for 'no joint ownership'; this is better characterised as compliant with the joint-ownership carve-out noted, but the rationale does disclose the joint ownership and the classification outcome is unchanged.
